name: SwampHacks
participants_note: 411 registered on Devpost; ages 18+, college students only. Co-hosted with Vobile.

prizes.name: Best Overall Sponsored By Vobile (1st, 2nd, & 3rd Place)
prizes.notes: Three winners; project pages do not show which placed first.

prizes.name: Best Education, Accessibility, & Social Impact Project
prizes.notes: Specialized track; teams may enter at most one.

prizes.name: Best Everyday Life & Wellbeing [Human-Centered Design] Project
Best Finance Hack Sponsored By Capital One
prizes.notes: Optional use of the sponsor's mock banking API.

prizes.name: Tender for Lawyers Sponsored By Morgan & Morgan
prizes.notes: An AI orchestrator that reads messy multi-channel legal inputs, finds the next action and routes it to AI specialists. Project pages do not show the order.

prizes.name: Best Beginner Hack
prizes.notes: At least half the team must be first-time hackers.

prizes.name: Best Creative Media
prizes.notes: Visual design, storytelling, animation, audio or interactive media.

prizes.name: GitHub: “Ship It” — Best Use of GitHub
prizes.notes: Requires a public repo with README, at least 10 commits, 3 pull requests with a review, 5 assigned issues and a release tag.

prizes.name: Hidden Challenge: Least Vibecoded Project - By CISE Professor
prizes.notes: Rewards clean, maintainable code and intentional engineering over hype.

prize_count_note: USD 11,500 in cash plus prizes in kind.

criteria.label: Technical Execution
criteria.description: How well it functions and is implemented, including how much was really built at the event.

criteria.label: Innovation & Creativity
criteria.description: Original idea or approach, or creative use of technology.

criteria.label: Impact & Purpose
criteria.description: Significance of the problem and the real-world value of the solution.

criteria.label: Clarity & Communication
criteria.description: How clearly the pitch and demo explain the problem, solution and technical decisions.

criteria.label: Completion & Scope
criteria.description: How complete it is for the timeframe; a working prototype rather than a concept.

criteria.label: Track & Challenge Relevance
criteria.description: Fit with the chosen track or sponsor challenge.

judging.judge_profile_summary: Judges are not named on the event page.
judging.notes: Sponsor challenges are judged only by sponsor-assigned judges. Judging happens at a project expo. Prototypes are allowed.

curator_notes: All 22 prize winners are analyzed records. The three Best Overall winners are podium without rank because project pages do not say which placed first. Two criteria share the challenge-relevance lens (completion and track fit). Taglines are CrafterWIKI paraphrases; domains assigned conservatively.
